default: Check visitor centre opening hours and whether trails need advance booking.
Carry layers — mountain parks can be much colder than nearby towns.
Pack water and snacks; facilities can be sparse inside large protected areas.
Stay on marked paths to protect fragile habitats and avoid fines.
Download offline maps — mobile signal is often weak in valleys and forests.
Montenegro: Park entry fees are often paid in cash at gates — carry euros and small notes.
Mountain roads to Durmitor and Biogradska Gora can be narrow; allow extra drive time.
Lovćen’s mausoleum road has many switchbacks — check opening hours before sunset drives.
Wild camping is restricted; use marked campsites or guesthouses in gateway villages.
Croatia: Some parks sell timed entry tickets online in peak season — book ahead.
Swimming is only allowed in designated areas at lake parks.
Iceland: Weather changes fast; road access to trailheads may close without warning.
Ferry or 4×4 may be needed for remote sectors — check park website.
Norway: DNT cabins and marked trails follow Norwegian trekking customs — respect quiet hours.
Parking at popular trailheads fills early in July and August.
